page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 32.0 GB of system memory. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU performance is generally weak to average, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25 percent, and stress-ng multi-core performance ranking in the middle 50 percent. However, the system excels in LLM inference benchmarks. For both small (135M) and medium (7B) models, prompt processing and text generation speeds rank in the top 10 percent tier, demonstrating the high efficiency of the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU for machine learning tasks.

Given the weak single-core CPU performance and average memory bandwidth, using this instance for pure CPU-bound computing or standard software compilation is not cost-efficient. Instead, its value lies in GPU-accelerated workloads. The g2-standard-8 is highly suited for low-to-medium parameter LLM inference, graphics rendering, and machine learning model deployment where GPU acceleration offsets the modest CPU capabilities.
